I scanned the LSP server in vsec and the VS Code client, then compared against vsrocq and Proof General.

### Implemented in vsec today

- LSP server (`src/eclsp/lspManager.ml`):
  - initialize: advertises textDocumentSync, completion, hover, definition, references. Also advertises semanticTokensProvider via raw JSON (range + full).
  - completion: basic keywords list; also a fast-path JSON handler for `textDocument/completion`.
  - hover: DocumentManager-backed; with robust word-based fallback.
  - definition: DocumentManager-backed; with regex-based fallback.
  - references: DocumentManager-backed (returns same-document locations).
  - diagnostics: published on state updates; plus heuristic extra diagnostics for certain lines.
  - semantic tokens: custom EasyCrypt analysis generates tokens; supports both full and range requests; returns standard LSP encoded data; also sends a custom notification `vsec/semanticHighlighting`.
  - execution overview: custom `prover/executionOverview`.
  - proof state: custom `prover/proofView`.
  - messages: custom `prover/messages`.
  - document lifecycle: didOpen/Change/Close; background interpretation; state management.
- VS Code extension client (`vscode-extension/src/extension.ts`, `src/client.ts`, `src/panels/GoalPanel.ts`, goal-view-ui):
  - LanguageClient created and started; toolchain manager launches `vsec-lsp`.
  - Receives server custom notifications: `vsec/semanticHighlighting`, `prover/proofView`, `prover/executionOverview`, `prover/messages`.
  - Applies semantic highlighting via VS Code decorations (not via VS Code built-in semantic tokens API).
  - Goal panel webview with an LSP bridge that forwards:
    - textDocument/semanticTokens/full, /range
    - textDocument/hover
    - textDocument/completion
  - Interactive proving commands: `vsec.showGoalPanel`, `vsec.stepForward`, `vsec.stepBackward`, `vsec.interpretToPoint`, `vsec.interpretToEnd`, proof search.
  - No registration of VS Code built-ins like code actions, rename, references UI, etc.; these rely on LanguageClient default wiring if server supports.

### Reference: vsrocq
- Server (`vsrocqtop/lspManager.ml`) advertises and implements:
  - textDocumentSync, completion, hover, definition, documentSymbol.
  - diagnostics, proof/execution notifications similar to vsec.
  - No semantic tokens in capabilities (in this file).
- Client registers many commands and a code actions provider; more complete command set and UI integration.

### Reference: Proof General (PG)
- PG is not an LSP; no LSP features to compare. It provides rich IDE features via its own protocol.

### Gaps and partially implemented features in vsec vs typical LSP IntelliSense set

- Semantic tokens:
  - Server: implemented with full/range responses and legend via raw JSON in initialize.
  - Client: NOT using VS Code semantic tokens provider; instead consumes a custom `vsec/semanticHighlighting` notification and applies decorations. This bypasses theme-aware, token-legend-based coloring. Missing using `languages.registerDocumentSemanticTokensProvider` on client or relying on LanguageClient semantic tokens wiring. Partial.
- Document symbols:
  - Server: not implemented in EasyCrypt LSP (comment says “will implement later”). Missing.
  - Client: no symbol features wired. Missing.
- Workspace symbols:
  - Server/Client: not present. Missing.
- Rename:
  - Server: no `textDocument/rename`. Missing.
  - Client: no rename UI integration. Missing.
- Code actions:
  - Server: no `textDocument/codeAction`. Missing.
  - Client: no provider or middleware. Missing.
- Signature help (parameter hints):
  - Server: no `textDocument/signatureHelp`. Missing.
  - Client: not registered. Missing.
- Inlay hints:
  - Server: none. Client: none. Missing.
- Formatting (document/range/on-type):
  - Server: none. Client: none. Missing.
- References:
  - Server: implemented for same-document; not clear on cross-file navigation or workspace index. Partial.
  - Client: relies on generic LanguageClient behavior; no custom UI.
- Go to type/implementation:
  - Not implemented. Missing.
- Folding ranges, selection ranges, color provider, linked editing, call hierarchy, semantic tokens delta, diagnostic pull model:
  - Not implemented. Missing.
- Completion:
  - Implemented minimally; no resolve, no context-aware completions. Partial.
- Hover:
  - Implemented with fallback; decent. Partial (no markup links to docs, types, etc.).
- Diagnostics:
  - Implemented; includes heuristic additional diagnostics. OK.
- Semantic tokens refresh:
  - Server sends `workspace/semanticTokens/refresh`. Client does not register a semantic tokens provider to handle it. Partial.
- Multi-file/project awareness:
  - Definition/references appear document-scoped; no workspace symbol index or cross-file nav. Partial.

### Compared to vsrocq
- vsec adds semantic tokens and the custom goal/execution/messages webview integration, which vsrocq file doesn’t show for semantic tokens.
- vsec lacks documentSymbol (present in vsrocq), and likely has fewer code actions and integrated UI commands than vsrocq’s client.

### Actionable list of not-fully-implemented items in vsec
- Use VS Code semantic tokens API on the client and remove reliance on ad-hoc `vsec/semanticHighlighting`.
- Implement server handlers and advertise capabilities for:
  - documentSymbol and workspaceSymbol
  - rename
  - codeAction
  - signatureHelp
  - inlayHints
  - formatting (document/range/onType)
  - foldingRange, selectionRange
  - typeDefinition, implementation, references across files
- Improve completion: context-aware items, resolve provider.
- Cross-file symbols/indexing for definition/references.
- Wire LanguageClient semanticTokens plumbing formally (drop raw JSON initialize path when bindings are available).

Let me know if you want me to:
- draft the concrete server-side edits for documentSymbol and rename, or
- add a proper DocumentSemanticTokensProvider on the client to consume the server’s semanticTokens/full|range.
